author: WPB1
summary: Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e) of module ownership, the Game lifecycle, GraphicsDeviceManager/GameWindow and the math and core types. Nearly all of its current substance is already on the framework deep dives (lifecycle, timestep, shutdown, components, window/manager, math conventions, layout, numerics, bounding volumes, colour, curves) and the runtime/math/core internals, often in corrected form (platform window facade, Letterbox default, Asyncify web loop, wider-than-float arithmetic, oracle tests). The residue added is the static-initialisation-order caveat for the math constants.

concepts.text: Game's constructor value-constructs a complete GraphicsDevice member before any GraphicsDeviceManager exists and binds the window and ContentManager to it: the largest structural divergence from FNA, where the manager creates the device.

concepts.text: Game constructor defaults: InactiveSleepTime 20 ms, IsActive false, IsFixedTimeStep true, IsMouseVisible false, TargetElapsedTime of 166,667 ticks (1/60 s), a 1 ms initial sleep-precision estimate.

concepts.text: ~Game() runs Dispose(false), which skips component disposal, Content disposal, graphics-service disposal and the gamepad shutdown, so destruction alone never runs the explicit lifecycle callbacks.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Run() is AssertNotDisposed, one-time DoInitialize, BeginRun, BeforeLoop, the loop, EndRun, AfterLoop; it does not reset the exit flag, so a second Run() after Exit() runs no ticks but still raises Exiting and the Begin/End hooks.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: RunOneFrame() initialises and ticks once without BeginRun, BeforeLoop, EndRun, AfterLoop or Exiting, so IsActive stays false throughout because only BeforeLoop sets it.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Exit() only requests the stop (and suppresses the current frame's draw); Exiting is raised after the loop ends and before EndRun()/AfterLoop(), so an Exiting handler runs before an EndRun override.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: ResetElapsedTime() has an effect only under variable timestep; SuppressDraw() sets a flag consumed once at the end of the tick; BeginDraw() returning false skips both Draw and EndDraw, and without a manager EndDraw presents the device directly.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Timing: alpha.1 read SDL_GetPerformanceCounter through double milliseconds; at this snapshot the loop reads the platform clock service, still comparing through the same adaptive-sleep scheme.
concepts.note: Corrected: platform clock abstraction replaces direct SDL calls.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Fixed-step waiting is FNA's two-phase adaptive sleep: 1 ms sleeps while the remaining time exceeds the worst measured sleep, then a yield spin; each sleep sample is capped at 4 ms in a 128-entry ring rescanned only when the evicted sample was the worst.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: MaxElapsedTime (500 ms) clamps accumulated time after the event pump and before the update loop, bounding catch-up updates per frame; input is pumped after the pacing wait and before Update.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Under fixed step Update sees ElapsedGameTime equal to the target, but after the loop ElapsedGameTime is rewritten to target times step count in integer ticks, so Draw sees the whole tick's game time.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: IsRunningSlowly is a five-step lag counter with hysteresis (set at 5, cleared only at 0, decremented on single-step ticks), never written by the variable-step branch.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Variable timestep: a forced zero leaves TotalGameTime unadvanced; otherwise elapsed equals accumulated time and exactly one Update runs.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: GameTime holds TotalGameTime, ElapsedGameTime and IsRunningSlowly with public getters and setters reserved to Game.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Game::Update and Draw iterate a snapshot of the component lists, so adding or removing components during iteration is safe; order changes re-sort through event subscriptions installed at categorisation.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Game::Update calls FrameworkDispatcher::Update() after the component loop, so an Update override that does not call the base silently stops dynamic audio, media and touch dispatch.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Components are ordered by a sorted insert before the first strictly greater order (lower first, equal values in insertion order); components added before DoInitialize are categorised by its loop, not by the ComponentAdded handler.

concepts.text: GameComponentTests.cpp and DrawableGameComponentTests.cpp contain no tests because a live Game is needed; component behaviour is source-read.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: GameServiceContainer maps std::type_index of the explicitly named interface to a pointer adjusted at the call site, which keeps multiple-inheritance lookups correct; it is non-owning, rejects null and duplicate keys with std::invalid_argument, silently ignores removal of an absent key and is move-only; tests pin non-primary-base adjustment.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: GraphicsDeviceManager implements the three-method IGraphicsDeviceManager (BeginDraw, CreateDevice, EndDraw) and IGraphicsDeviceService; its Game constructor deliberately does not call ApplyChanges (double reconfiguration flicker) and registers under both service keys, a second manager throwing.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: The ClientSizeChanged handler only refreshes the viewport and never calls ApplyChanges, because feeding the physical window size in as the virtual resolution would corrupt logical coordinates.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Manager defaults: Reach profile, windowed, no multisampling, SurfaceFormat::Color, 800x480, Depth24, vsync on; the CNA-only presentation mode defaulted to FixedHeightDynamicWidth at alpha.1 and defaults to Letterbox at this snapshot.
concepts.note: Corrected default presentation mode (Letterbox).

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: PresentationMode is a CNAEXT enum declared beside the manager with five values; PresentationParameters has no such field and the mode reaches the renderer out of band, before the reset.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: ApplyChanges() returns early unless a preference changed; CreateDevice/ApplyChanges build the device information, raise PreparingDeviceSettings last so handler changes survive, bracket the window change, then apply profile, presentation mode, an in-place Reset and a viewport refresh.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Preference mapping: vsync to PresentInterval One or Immediate; multisampling to 0 or a hard-coded 8 (FNA queries the device maximum); portrait size swap only on iOS and Android.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: The manager forwards the device's own reset events (subscribed once after the settle-in reset, so start-up raises only DeviceCreated), re-raises DeviceDisposing/Reset/Resetting with itself as sender while DeviceCreated keeps the original, and raises DeviceDisposing ungated by device ownership.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: CanResetDevice, FindBestDevice and RankDevices return defaults instead of FNA's NotImplementedException and are called by nothing; CreateDevice throws without a Game-owned device; BeginDraw returns false when no device can draw.

concepts.text: GameWindow was one concrete SDL3 class reading SDL live with cached fallbacks, whose setters threw std::runtime_error on SDL failure and which exposed an SDL-typed window accessor.
concepts.note: Corrected: GameWindow is a facade over CNA::Platform::IPlatformWindow; SDL3 failures become PlatformException; the SDL accessor was replaced by GetNativeWindowHandleEXT.

concepts.text: One window query is deliberately non-fatal: the client-bounds query keeps the last good rectangle instead of throwing, covering the browser canvas start-up race.

concepts.text: FrameworkDispatcher::Update() snapshots the stream list under its mutex and updates each stream with the lock released, because a BufferNeeded handler may dispose its own stream and the mutex is not recursive.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: LaunchParameters publicly inherits std::unordered_map (no virtual destructor), reads the command line on Windows and Linux/Android only, and parses FNA-style key:value arguments with first occurrence winning.

concepts.text: TitleContainer::OpenStream throws std::runtime_error and logs per call; ReadToPointer returns a malloc'd buffer freed by FreePointer; TitleLocation resolves lazily with unsynchronised statics.

concepts.text: ExitingEventArgs exists as an empty type that Game never uses; Game::Exiting is an EventHandler<System::EventArgs>, as in XNA 4.0.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: Under Emscripten at alpha.1 RunLoop called emscripten_set_main_loop with simulateInfiniteLoop, so Run never returned and EndRun/AfterLoop never ran.
concepts.note: At TARGET the browser loop suspends the Wasm stack between frames (Asyncify), so Run returns as on the desktop; the site states the current loop.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: The browser frame body is a separate loop that stores the game in a static (one Game per process), uses a millisecond clock, caps the frame delta at 250 ms, always runs fixed steps and forces IsRunningSlowly false.

concepts.text: The alpha.1 lifetime hazard of a stack-allocated Game under Emscripten (-fwasm-exceptions catching the unwind throw and destroying locals) and its documentation.

concepts.section: PART 1 — FACTS: GAME LIFECYCLE AND FRAMEWORK CORE
concepts.text: The runtime module throws only standard exception types (out_of_range, invalid_argument, runtime_error including use after dispose, logic_error, bad_alloc), never a System type.
concepts.note: Site count is 21 explicit throw sites at TARGET (30 at alpha.1).

concepts.text: System::Exception derives from std::exception, not std::runtime_error, so only catch (const std::exception&) spans both the standard and the System families.

concepts.section: LIFECYCLE ORDER (exact, cited)
concepts.text: Phase A, construction: members in declaration order (a real device is created), window bound to the renderer's window, content bound to the device, one FrameworkDispatcher::Update, audio initialisation; a manager then registers its services without applying changes.

concepts.section: LIFECYCLE ORDER (exact, cited)
concepts.text: Phase B, Run to first Draw: DoInitialize resolves the manager, CreateDevice (PreparingDeviceSettings, window change, reset, DeviceCreated), initialises the gamepad subsystem so pre-connected pads are enumerated, calls Initialize (components, DeviceDisposing to UnloadContent subscription, LoadContent now or on DeviceCreated), categorises components, then BeginRun and BeforeLoop (Activated).

concepts.section: LIFECYCLE ORDER (exact, cited)
concepts.text: Phase C, one desktop tick: advance time, pace (fixed step), pump events (quit, debug context-loss keys, resize, focus to Activated/Deactivated), clamp, run updates, then draw unless suppressed.

concepts.section: LIFECYCLE ORDER (exact, cited)
concepts.text: Phase D, shutdown: Exit sets the stop flag and suppresses the draw, Exiting fires, EndRun and AfterLoop run; Dispose() disposes components, content and the graphics service (DeviceDisposing, then UnloadContent), shuts the gamepad subsystem, marks disposed and raises Disposed.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Vectors, Matrix, Quaternion, Plane, Ray, Point, Rectangle and the Curve types have no polymorphic bases, while Color, BoundingBox, BoundingSphere, BoundingFrustum and CurveKey derive from interfaces with virtual functions and so carry vtable pointers (IEquatable<T>, and IPackedVectorT for Color).

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: sizeof(Color) is not 4 (CNA's comments record 24 on 64-bit builds), so Color arrays must never be reinterpreted as RGBA bytes and vertex types cannot be uploaded by copying sizeof(T) bytes.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: The math module type-puns through std::memcpy in a file-local FloatHash duplicated in the three vector files, not through std::bit_cast; there is no SIMD.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Only Vector2 has a constexpr constructor and constinit constants; Vector3, Vector4, Quaternion::Identity, Point, Rectangle and Color constants are dynamically initialised, so a static initialiser elsewhere can copy zeros; Matrix identity is a function-local static.

target.evidence: modules/math/src/Vector2.cpp, Vector3.cpp, Vector4.cpp, Quaternion.cpp, Color.cpp, Matrix.cpp (getIdentityProperty) at 009d40f5

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: MathHelper::MachineEpsilonFloat is computed at dynamic initialisation by halving (2^-24), used by WithinEpsilon, Ray, Curve tangents and the key collection; a static-time consumer could see 0.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Arithmetic precision: alpha.1 said everything was float except the MathHelper interpolators and one BoundingBox accumulation, and that Matrix::Invert declined FNA's double widening; at this snapshot Multiply, Invert, Vector3 transforms and CreateFromPoints are evaluated wider than float to match XNA's x87 results.
concepts.note: Corrected by CNA's oracle-driven changes after alpha.1.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Right-handed basis with Forward = (0,0,-1) and Up = (0,1,0); no LH/RH variants; every angle is in radians.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Matrix stores sixteen named row-major floats (no array or operator[]), default-constructs to zero rather than identity, and has no Identity object, only getIdentityProperty(); Quaternion::Identity is a real constant.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Row-vector convention: Matrix::Multiply(A, B) applies A first and translation sits in row 4; Quaternion::Multiply(q1, q2) applies q2 first (Concatenate(a, b) equals Multiply(b, a)), the opposite argument order.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Projection builders map depth to [0, 1] (Direct3D), independently confirmed by BoundingFrustum's plane extraction, which yields outward-facing planes.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Matrix::ToColumnMajor (CNAEXT) copies fields in declaration order and does not transpose; the transpose is the GL/Vulkan reading, and its only test uses the identity.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Vector3::Transform by a matrix neither reads the fourth column nor divides by w; TransformNormal uses the matrix itself (not the inverse transpose) and exists only for Vector2/Vector3.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: CreateFromYawPitchRoll composes roll about Z, then pitch about X, then yaw about Y about fixed axes.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Plane is Normal·X + D = 0, so D is the negated origin distance; only the three-point constructor normalises; DotCoordinate is the signed distance.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: BoundingBox::GetCorners returns XNA's order (Max.Z face first, Max at index 1, Min at index 7) and the frustum corners follow the same topology; no test asserts either order.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Degenerate inputs are silent: zero-vector, zero-quaternion and zero-normal-plane normalisation give NaN, a singular Invert fills with inf/NaN, Reflect with a zero normal returns the input; only the perspective builders validate arguments, and the field-of-view guard 3.141593f admits exactly Pi.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: The private CheckForNaNs helpers and getDebugDisplayStringProperty are ported XNA debugging aids with no callers.
concepts.note: Recorded by the Known Issues pipeline as not a bug (CNA-BUG-042).

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Equality is exact float comparison everywhere (a NaN vector is unequal to itself, q and -q differ, BoundingFrustum compares only its matrix); WithinEpsilon exists but no Equals uses it.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: MathHelper and the vector types disagree for same-named functions: SmoothStep/Hermite endpoint shortcuts and double evaluation, and inverted-range Clamp (min wins in MathHelper, max wins per component), plus NaN behaviour of Max/Min.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: MathHelper::Lerp is the imprecise a + (b - a)t; CNA tracks FNA rather than MonoGame (no LerpPrecise or power-of-two helpers) and makes three FNA-internal helpers public: Clamp(int), WithinEpsilon, ClosestMSAAPower.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: WrapAngle returns the half-open range (-Pi, Pi].

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Ray uses different tolerances per target (WithinEpsilon for the box slabs, 1e-5 for planes, none for spheres), returns std::optional<float>, and a zero-direction ray inside a box returns no hit.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Curve::ComputeTangent tests degeneracy against two different epsilons for the in and out tangents, and Evaluate's Linear post-loop uses the first key's TangentOut.
concepts.note: Both recorded by the Known Issues pipeline (CNA-BUG-028, NEW-B1-09).

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Curve evaluation is cubic Hermite with tangents in value per segment, a Step branch and loop types; CurveKeyCollection inserts before the first strictly greater position (duplicates allowed) and its setter can move an element.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: BoundingSphere::CreateFromPoints was described at alpha.1 as Ritter's algorithm checked only for enclosure; at this snapshot it reproduces XNA's own two-pass algorithm bit for bit against 445 recorded point sets, and CreateFromBoundingBox is the circumscribed sphere.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Rectangle::Contains is half-open, Intersects is strict (touching rectangles do not intersect, unlike boxes), IsEmpty needs all four fields zero, Center uses integer division, and there is no Contains(Vector2).

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Point stores int32 X/Y with component-wise operators that XNA's Point lacks.
concepts.note: Alpha.1 said Point had zero Vector interop; the site states the TARGET surface.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Operator sets and conversions: widening constructors only, no conversion operators, no operator<< (streaming uses ToString), and ToString brace styles that follow FNA per type (pinned by ToStringMatchesFNAFormat).

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Color has 141 static constants: 140 opaque named colours plus Transparent, and 139 distinct packed values because Aqua/Cyan and Fuchsia/Magenta alias.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Color packs A<<24 | B<<16 | G<<8 | R (RGBA bytes in memory on little-endian); constructors clamp and truncate with NaN to 0, PackFromVector4 truncates without clamping like FNA, and there is no rounding.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: FromNonPremultiplied multiplies RGB by alpha (integer overload with integer division); Multiply scales all four channels; Lerp clamps its amount; named constants are stored straight.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Math test evidence at alpha.1: 818 flat TEST cases, three tolerance literals, a looser kEps in BoundingFrustumTests, and no XNA numeric oracle anywhere.
concepts.note: Corrected: 873 static definitions and two oracle suites (MatrixOracleTests, BoundingSphereOracleTests) at TARGET.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES
concepts.text: Semantics the math tests do not pin: multiplication-order contrasts, ToColumnMajor transposition (identity input), corner order, singular inversion, zero-vector normalisation and NaN handling.

concepts.section: PART 2 — FACTS: MATH AND CORE TYPES

concepts.section: ★ NEW FINDING: a live correctness bug in Plane::Transform(Plane, Matrix)
concepts.text: Plane::Transform(plane, matrix) inverts and then calls Matrix::Transpose with one object as source and destination; that overload is not alias-safe and symmetrises from the lower triangle, so a translation tilts the plane; the only tests use the identity.
concepts.note: Published through Known Issues as CNA-BUG-001; the page carries the worked counterexample and a workaround.

concepts.section: ★ NEW FINDING: a live correctness bug in Plane::Transform(Plane, Matrix)
concepts.text: Blast radius: every other Matrix::Transpose caller uses the value-returning overload, so only the plane-by-matrix transform is affected.

concepts.section: MODULE OWNERSHIP (answering "locate precisely which module owns what")
